session.question: How sustainability reporting link with SDGs and sustainability performance, it matter from the supply chain framework too?
session.answer:
Sustainability reporting links directly to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by translating corporate activities into reported contributions, impacts, and trade-offs relative to the 17 goals. In the cited frameworks, reporting is not only descriptive; it is intended to align disclosed metrics with SDG commitments, stakeholder expectations, and broader sustainable development outcomes. Better sustainability performance is associated with stronger disclosure, particularly for environmental and social dimensions, suggesting that reporting can reflect underlying performance and also signal it to external audiences. (nicolo2023doessdgdisclosure chunk 1, kucukgul2021enhancingthevalue chunk 1, abeysekera2022aframeworkfor chunk 1)

The relationship matters from a supply chain perspective because supply chains are a major locus of sustainability impacts and performance leverage. The digital transformation study shows that supply chain concentration mediates the effect of digital transformation on sustainable performance: more digitalized firms tend to have less concentrated, more diversified supply chains, which is associated with improved triple-bottom-line outcomes and SDG-aligned performance. This indicates that supply chain structure can materially shape sustainability performance and should be part of sustainability reporting and strategy. (le2024sustainableperformancemeasurement chunk 1)

A life cycle sustainability assessment (LCSA)-based framework further strengthens this link by integrating environmental, social, governance (ESG) factors with life-cycle impacts across products and systems, including in supply-chain-relevant contexts such as oil and gas. It is designed to identify sustainability issues across the life cycle and support SDG-aligned improvements, showing that reporting frameworks can be extended beyond firm boundaries to capture upstream and downstream impacts. (padilla‐rivera2024enhancingenvironmentalsocial chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-8388bd1c: The excerpt describes a 2024 paper proposing a framework that integrates Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment (LCSA) impact categories with Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors to improve ESG assessment and reporting. The framework is meant to align reporting with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by enabling detailed evaluation of environmental, economic, and social performance across product and system life cycles. It also incorporates the UN’s 10 principles and is presented as adaptable across industries. A theoretical application in Canada’s oil and gas sector is used to show how the framework can identify sustainability issues and provide actionable insights for SDG-aligned performance improvements. The excerpt emphasizes conceptual and practical links, but does not report empirical results.
From Alejandro Padilla‐Rivera, Marwa Hannouf, Getachew Assefa, and Ian D. Gates. Enhancing environmental, social, and governance, performance and reporting through integration of life cycle sustainability assessment framework. Sustainable Development, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/sd.3265, doi:10.1002/sd.3265.

pqac-078848f3: The excerpt describes a conceptual sustainability reporting framework that uses the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as “goal posts” for reporting sustainability outcomes and impacts. It argues that many existing sustainability reporting frameworks overemphasize sustainability performance and inter-firm comparisons, whereas this proposed principle-based approach focuses on how firms demonstrate their chosen contribution to sustainable development. The framework is grounded in Gaia Theory and the Theory of Distributive Justice, emphasizing fair acquisition and use of resources to support life within habitable limits. It is intended to integrate with financial and economic intellectual capital reporting and is framed as a joint project between firms and stakeholders. The paper is conceptual, so it does not report empirical findings; instead, it calls for future empirical validation. No supply-chain-specific framework details appear in this excerpt.
From Indra Abeysekera. A framework for sustainability reporting. Sustainability Accounting Management and Policy Journal, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1108/sampj-08-2021-0316, doi:10.1108/sampj-08-2021-0316.

pqac-77afe469: The excerpt discusses how corporate sustainability reporting frameworks have increasingly included guidance to support companies’ commitments to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The paper argues that corporations struggle to use these guides effectively, and proposes an alignment approach to harmonize GRI and IIRC SDGs guides so companies can better meet SDGs reporting challenges. Conceptually, the link is that sustainability reporting can improve SDGs performance by helping firms align reporting deliverables with SDGs commitments and stakeholder expectations. Empirically, the paper examines four telecommunication companies’ sustainability assessment and reporting performance and concludes that using the proposed alignment framework can increase SDGs reporting performance. It does not mention a supply chain framework.
From Egemen Kücükgül, Pontus Cerin, and Yang Liu. Enhancing the value of corporate sustainability: an approach for aligning multiple sdgs guides on reporting. Journal of Cleaner Production, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2021.130005, doi:10.1016/j.jclepro.2021.130005.

pqac-1f2fa922: The excerpt describes a 2024 study that builds a conceptual framework linking digital transformation, supply chain concentration, and sustainable performance within the sustainable development framework. It argues that prior literature lacks detailed analysis of how these dimensions interact. Based on stakeholder theory and data from 3,947 listed Chinese firms, the study finds that digital transformation is positively associated with improved sustainable performance measured by the triple bottom line, supporting SDGs 8 and 9. A key mechanism is that digital transformation reduces supply chain concentration and encourages a more diversified supply chain configuration, which helps explain the performance gains. The study also reports significant heterogeneity in the digital transformation–sustainable performance relationship, and suggests policy support for digital transformation and diversified supply chains.
From Sun Le, Tze San Ong, Boon Heng Teh, and Assunta Di Vaio. Sustainable performance measurement through digital transformation within the sustainable development framework: the mediating effect of supply chain concentration. Sustainable Development, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/sd.3007, doi:10.1002/sd.3007.

pqac-761a74a2: The excerpt discusses a 2023 study on whether SDG disclosure reflects firms’ underlying sustainability performance. It frames the UN 2030 Agenda and SDGs as creating pressure for firms to integrate SDG concerns into operations and to improve transparency. The study uses 635 companies across 45 countries (2016–2020), measuring SDG disclosure from UN Global Compact Communication on Progress (CoP) questionnaires and sustainability performance with Refinitiv Eikon ESG scores. Panel Tobit regressions show that higher sustainability performance, especially environmental and social performance, is positively associated with greater SDG disclosure. The authors interpret this as support for voluntary disclosure theory: better performers disclose more to signal their quality to investors and stakeholders. The excerpt does not mention supply chain frameworks.
From Giuseppe Nicolò, Giovanni Zampone, Serena De Iorio, and Giuseppe Sannino. Does sdg disclosure reflect corporate underlying sustainability performance? evidence from un global compact participants. Journal of International Financial Management and Accounting, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1111/jifm.12194, doi:10.1111/jifm.12194.

contexts.context: The excerpt is about green supply chain management (GSCM) research and its explicit mapping to the UN SDGs, not sustainability reporting. It reports that GSCM publications  were mapped to 17 SDGs using bibliometric and science-mapping methods. The most linked SDGs were SDG 9, SDG 12, and SDG 17. The thematic areas connected to sustainability outcomes include Industry 4.0 and sustainable supply chains, coordination of GSCM practices, environmental policy management, circular economy integration, sustainable sourcing, supply chain resilience, digital transformation, and performance monitoring. The study suggests that sustainability is increasingly integrated into supply chain processes and that environmental management and new technologies support SDG-related performance.
contexts.question: How does sustainability reporting link with the SDGs and sustainability performance, and does the supply chain framework matter? Focus on conceptual links, mechanisms, and any empirical findings.

contexts.context: The excerpt is about supply chain resilience, sustainability, and supply chain performance, not sustainability reporting or the SDGs directly. It does, however, provide a conceptual link showing that supply chain resilience improves supply chain sustainability (economic, social, environmental), and that sustainability then positively affects supply chain performance. The study finds no direct positive effect of resilience on performance; instead, sustainability mediates the relationship, creating a strong indirect effect. The paper emphasizes risk prevention, risk culture, integrating supply chains, and selecting partners with green performance as mechanisms for improving sustainability and performance. This is relevant only insofar as it suggests a supply-chain-based framework for sustainability outcomes.
contexts.question: How does sustainability reporting link with the SDGs and sustainability performance, and does the supply chain framework matter? Focus on conceptual links, mechanisms, and any empirical findings.

contexts.context: The excerpt is a bibliometric/science-mapping study on sustainability reporting (SR) and its links to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It reports that SR has grown sharply after 2015 alongside SDG awareness, and that SR research maps strongly to SDG 8 (decent work), SDG 9 (industry innovation), and SDG 12 (responsible consumption). The study identifies conceptual clusters around stakeholder engagement, corporate governance, accountability, climate change, and global reporting initiatives, and uses social network analysis to show SDG 9 and 12 as central. It also highlights future SR topics such as environmentally preferable purchasing, environmental management systems, education for sustainability, and green computing. However, it does not discuss supply chain frameworks or direct empirical links to sustainability performance.
contexts.question: How does sustainability reporting link with the SDGs and sustainability performance, and does the supply chain framework matter? Focus on conceptual links, mechanisms, and any empirical findings.

contexts.context: The excerpt is a 2022 review of supply chain collaboration (SCC) and sustainable development goals (SDGs), not specifically sustainability reporting. It says the literature at the SCC–sustainability intersection is mapped through a systematic review and identifies nine themes. Key mechanisms for SCC include collaborative innovation and collaborative process/product development. The paper argues that stronger SCC strategies can improve sustainable operational performance by increasing capacity building and resource utilisation. It also proposes a conceptual framework linking SCC to SDGs using a contingency approach. The abstract notes a gap: the literature has paid limited attention to the effectiveness of SCC mechanisms or their performance, implying little empirical evidence on outcomes.
contexts.question: How does sustainability reporting link with the SDGs and sustainability performance, and does the supply chain framework matter? Focus on conceptual links, mechanisms, and any empirical findings.

contexts.context: The excerpt discusses sustainable supply chain management (SSCM), technology adoption, and performance measurement as ways to promote sustainability and improve supply chain performance. It reports that the review found a lack of concrete frameworks for SSCM and a need for clearer, more applicable sustainability measurement indices. To address this, the authors proposed a framework for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through SSCM, along with a framework for deploying sustainability indicators. The abstract suggests that sustainability reporting/measurement is conceptually linked to sustainable development and performance improvement via indicators and digital-based supply chains, but it does not provide empirical results. The supply chain framework matters because the paper argues it is needed to operationalize SDG-oriented sustainability measurement in practice.
contexts.question: How does sustainability reporting link with the SDGs and sustainability performance, and does the supply chain framework matter? Focus on conceptual links, mechanisms, and any empirical findings.

contexts.context: The excerpt is about logistics firms in Nigeria and examines how supply chain leadership, digital supply chain practices, and corporate sustainability strategies affect sustainability performance. It finds that proactive sustainability strategies positively strengthen the relationship between supply chain leadership and sustainability performance, while reactive strategies weaken it. Digital supply also mediates the effects on sustainability performance. However, the excerpt does not mention sustainability reporting or any explicit relationship to SDG alignment, so it does not provide direct evidence on that question.
contexts.question: What is the relationship between sustainability reporting and supply chain sustainability performance, especially in relation to SDG alignment?

contexts.context: The excerpt discusses how supply chain resilience affects supply chain performance through the mediating effect of sustainability. It reports that supply chain resilience has a positive effect on supply chain sustainability, including economic, social, and environmental sustainability, and that supply chain sustainability positively affects supply chain performance. However, resilience does not directly improve performance; its effect is indirect via sustainability. The paper emphasizes building risk awareness, integrating supply chains, and focusing on green performance to promote sustainable development. It does not specifically mention sustainability reporting or SDG alignment, so no direct evidence is provided on that relationship.
contexts.question: What is the relationship between sustainability reporting and supply chain sustainability performance, especially in relation to SDG alignment?

contexts.context: The excerpt is about whether SDG disclosure reflects underlying corporate sustainability performance. Using 635 companies across 45 countries (2016–2020), the study finds a positive relationship: higher ESG sustainability performance leads to more SDG disclosure, with particularly strong effects through environmental and social performance. The paper argues that better sustainability performers disclose more SDG information to signal their quality to investors and stakeholders. It does not specifically discuss supply chain sustainability performance, but it suggests that sustainability reporting tends to be aligned with actual sustainability performance and thus may indicate genuine SDG commitment rather than purely symbolic disclosure.
contexts.question: What is the relationship between sustainability reporting and supply chain sustainability performance, especially in relation to SDG alignment?

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How sustainability reporting link with SDGs and sustainability performance, it matter from the supply chain framework too?

Sustainability reporting links directly to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by translating corporate activities into reported contributions, impacts, and trade-offs relative to the 17 goals. In the cited frameworks, reporting is not only descriptive; it is intended to align disclosed metrics with SDG commitments, stakeholder expectations, and broader sustainable development outcomes. Better sustainability performance is associated with stronger disclosure, particularly for environmental and social dimensions, suggesting that reporting can reflect underlying performance and also signal it to external audiences. (nicolo2023doessdgdisclosure chunk 1, kucukgul2021enhancingthevalue chunk 1, abeysekera2022aframeworkfor chunk 1)

The relationship matters from a supply chain perspective because supply chains are a major locus of sustainability impacts and performance leverage. The digital transformation study shows that supply chain concentration mediates the effect of digital transformation on sustainable performance: more digitalized firms tend to have less concentrated, more diversified supply chains, which is associated with improved triple-bottom-line outcomes and SDG-aligned performance. This indicates that supply chain structure can materially shape sustainability performance and should be part of sustainability reporting and strategy. (le2024sustainableperformancemeasurement chunk 1)

A life cycle sustainability assessment (LCSA)-based framework further strengthens this link by integrating environmental, social, governance (ESG) factors with life-cycle impacts across products and systems, including in supply-chain-relevant contexts such as oil and gas. It is designed to identify sustainability issues across the life cycle and support SDG-aligned improvements, showing that reporting frameworks can be extended beyond firm boundaries to capture upstream and downstream impacts. (padilla‐rivera2024enhancingenvironmentalsocial chunk 1)
